title: Marketing Mix Four Ps Overview
context: Review the marketing mix as a harmonised blend of product, price, place, and promotion tools. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A marketing mix is a harmonised blend of marketing tools that best meets the needs and wants of customers in the targeted market.
The marketing mix consists of only product and promotion because price and place are determined entirely by competitors.
Product is the least important element of the marketing mix because pricing decisions alone determine sales.
Place in the marketing mix refers primarily to the geographic location of the business headquarters.
The marketing mix consists of the four elements product, price, place, and promotion, commonly called the four Ps.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — The textbook defines the marketing mix as a coordinated blend of tools aligned with targeted customer needs.
FALSE — All four Ps—product, price, place, and promotion—form the marketing mix.
FALSE — Product is described as the most important decision and at the heart of marketing.
FALSE — Place concerns customer access and distribution, not the firm's headquarters location.
TRUE — Product, price, place, and promotion are the four Ps forming the marketing mix.

title: Harmonised Blend of Marketing Tools
context: Consider a regional ice-cream producer adding new flavours within its existing range and later introducing a yogurt line. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Promotion in the marketing mix means reducing the list price until stock is cleared from the warehouse.
A product line consists of completely unrelated goods such as laptops and restaurant meals grouped for accounting convenience.
Mix extension adds new variants within one existing line, such as another flavour in the same ice-cream range.
The basic idea of the marketing mix is to provide a good at an affordable price at a convenient place and communicate a message to promote sales.
Decisions across the four Ps of the marketing mix are based on market research findings about the targeted market.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Promotion covers communication tools such as advertising, not price cuts alone.
FALSE — A product line contains very similar products, not unrelated categories.
FALSE — That describes line extension; mix extension adds a new product line.
TRUE — Affordable price, convenient place, and promotional communication embody the core marketing-mix idea.
TRUE — Market research underpins marketing-mix decisions for the targeted market.

title: Product P at the Heart of Marketing
context: Review Figure 15 on the four elements of the marketing mix based on market research. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Line extension widens the product mix by adding an entirely new product line such as yogurts beside ice cream.
A relaunch always requires eliminating the product from the product line and replacing it with a new category.
Minor packaging changes are classified as mix extension because they alter how the product line is presented.
Each of the four Ps comprises several tools that marketers can combine within the overall marketing mix.
Brand loyalty is unrelated to the product element and belongs exclusively to the promotion P of the marketing mix.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Adding a new line is mix extension; line extension deepens one existing line.
FALSE — Relaunch involves minor changes such as packaging or colours, not automatic elimination.
FALSE — Minor packaging or colour changes are relaunches within alteration, not mix extension.
TRUE — Every P contains multiple tools that form part of the harmonised mix.
FALSE — Brands support differentiation within the product P and build loyalty there.

title: Product Lines and Mix Width
context: Analyze the product element of the marketing mix as the first P covering goods and services offered. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Brands consist only of production patents and contain no name, symbol, or sign visible to customers.
A harmonised marketing mix coordinates product, price, place, and promotion rather than treating each P independently.
The four Ps framework helps a business align what it sells, what it charges, where it is sold, and how it is promoted.
Marketing-mix planning seeks to satisfy targeted customers' needs and wants through a coordinated set of tools.
During introduction the product life cycle always shows peak profit because early buyers pay premium prices.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Brands include names, words, symbols, or signs distinguishing the product.
TRUE — The mix is harmonised across all four elements to meet customer needs.
TRUE — Product, price, place, and promotion cover offering, charge, distribution, and communication.
TRUE — Customer needs and wants in the target market guide the marketing mix.
FALSE — Introduction typically starts with losses from development and launch costs.

title: Brands and Product Differentiation
context: Consider a start-up launching an innovative fitness tracker with heavy advertising, low introductory prices, and online-only sales. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The product element of the marketing mix refers to all goods and services that are offered by a business.
The decline stage is characterised by the highest sales volume and peak profit in the product life cycle.
Product is at the heart of marketing and represents the most important decision of a business within the four Ps.
Maturity always lasts less than one year before every product automatically enters decline.
A question mark in the BCG matrix has high relative market share and low market growth.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — The first P covers every good and service the business offers.
FALSE — Decline features falling sales and profits, not peaks.
TRUE — The textbook places product at the centre as the most important marketing decision.
FALSE — Maturity can last months or years; some products remain mature indefinitely.
FALSE — Question marks have low relative share in a rapidly growing market.

title: Relaunch Versus Major Alteration
context: Analyze the role of brands in product differentiation, recognition, and loyalty within the product P. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Most businesses offer not just one product but a range of products within their portfolio.
Products that are very similar, such as several slightly different laptop computers, represent a product line.
A business can specialise in just one product line or diversify by offering different product lines such as laptops and monitors.
Increasing the number of different product lines widens the product mix of a business.
A star in the BCG matrix combines low relative market share with low market growth.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Businesses typically manage a portfolio of products rather than a single item.
TRUE — Similar variants like different laptops form one product line.
TRUE — Firms may focus on one line or diversify across multiple lines.
TRUE — Adding lines increases product-mix width through diversification.
FALSE — Stars have high relative share in a high-growth market.

title: Line Extension Within a Product Line
context: Review minor packaging and colour changes as a relaunch within product-mix alteration. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Offering only laptop computers illustrates specialising in a single product line within the product mix.
A cash cow has low relative market share in a rapidly growing market and requires heavy expansion investment.
A poor dog has high relative market share and high market growth and is the most valuable portfolio position.
The BCG matrix plots absolute market share against production cost per unit rather than relative share and growth.
Penetration pricing sets a very high initial price to skim revenue from early adopters only.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — A single-line focus is a product-mix specialisation strategy.
FALSE — Cash cows have high share in low-growth markets and usually receive lower investment.
FALSE — Poor dogs have low share and low growth near decline, unlike valuable stars.
FALSE — BCG uses relative market share and market growth, not cost per unit.
FALSE — High initial pricing describes skimming; penetration uses a low price to gain share.

title: Mix Extension Adding New Lines
context: Consider a beverage company using charm pricing on supermarket shelves and trade discounts for large retailers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Services such as technical support and online help count as products within the product element of the marketing mix.
Price skimming means launching with a low price to maximise volume in the first month of sales.
Packaging, labelling, and colour variants can form part of the product decision within the marketing mix.
Cost-plus pricing ignores production costs and sets price only according to competitor advertisements.
A business may offer goods, related services, and tailored software solutions as distinct products in its portfolio.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Services are included in the product P alongside physical goods.
FALSE — Skimming starts with a high price; low launch pricing aligns with penetration.
TRUE — Product decisions encompass packaging and presentation features.
FALSE — Cost-plus pricing adds a markup to production costs.
TRUE — Goods, services, and tailored solutions can each appear as products in the portfolio.

title: Product-Mix Expansion Strategies
context: Review product-mix strategies of expansion, alteration, and contraction in Figure 16. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Brands are created to support product differentiation within the product element of the marketing mix.
A brand consists of a name or a few words and/or a symbol and/or a sign that distinguishes a product or business.
Brands are intended to build a USP, brand recognition, and brand loyalty among customers.
Psychological pricing requires every product to be sold at a round number such as €10.00 without exception.
Wholesalers sell products directly to final consumers at retail shops they operate under their own brand only.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Brands help distinguish offerings and support differentiation.
TRUE — Brands combine names, words, symbols, or signs for distinction.
TRUE — Brands support USP, recognition, and loyalty objectives.
FALSE — Psychological pricing often uses charm prices like €9.99, not only round numbers.
FALSE — Wholesalers resell to retailers; retailers typically serve final consumers.

title: Product-Mix Alteration and Contraction
context: Analyze the product life cycle model of introduction, growth, maturity, and decline stages. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Some brands look the same worldwide with consistent colour and font to maintain global recognition.
Brands serve as a guarantee of stable quality and a maintained level of quality across markets.
Brands can render trust and safety of choice for customers who seek familiar products abroad.
Brand loyalty encourages customers to repurchase products associated with a trusted name or symbol.
A recognisable brand symbol can reinforce the USP communicated through the wider marketing mix.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Global brands use consistent visual identity across markets.
TRUE — Brands signal consistent quality standards to customers.
TRUE — Familiar brands provide reassurance and perceived safety when travelling.
TRUE — Loyalty flows from trusted brand identity and repeated satisfactory purchase.
TRUE — Symbols support USP communication within the product P.

title: Introduction Stage of Product Life Cycle
context: Consider a book publisher selling through bookshops, online platforms, and direct school supply contracts. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retailers purchase products in bulk from producers and resell exclusively to other wholesalers downstream.
Minor changes such as different packaging or colours are called a relaunch within product-mix alteration.
When a relaunch is not enough to keep customers satisfied, major changes or elimination from the line may be necessary.
Adding new products to an existing product line is a line extension, such as producing more flavours of ice cream.
Direct distribution always requires at least two intermediaries between producer and customer.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Retailers sell to end customers; bulk resale to other wholesalers is the wholesaler role.
TRUE — Relaunches involve minor packaging or colour changes rather than full redesign.
TRUE — Insufficient relaunches may require major alteration or product elimination.
TRUE — Line extension deepens an existing line with additional variants.
FALSE — Direct distribution sells without intermediaries.

title: Growth Stage Sales and Profit Patterns
context: Analyze the Boston Consulting Group matrix using relative market share and market growth. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Adding a new product line to the portfolio is a mix extension, such as yogurts in addition to ice cream.
Line extension increases the depth of a product line by adding variants within that line.
Indirect distribution means the producer delivers every product personally to each household without any retailer.
Online sales channels belong to the promotion P because they only advertise products without enabling purchase.
Mix extension increases the number of product lines offered by the business.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Mix extension widens the portfolio by adding a new line.
TRUE — Depth grows when more variants join one existing line.
FALSE — Indirect distribution uses intermediaries such as wholesalers and retailers.
FALSE — Online platforms are place channels that make products available for purchase.
TRUE — Width grows when a new line is added to the portfolio.

title: Maturity Stage Profit Peak
context: Review BCG categories of stars, question marks, cash cows, and poor dogs. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Personal selling is a price tool because sales staff negotiate discounts that permanently replace promotion.
Product-mix expansion can occur through line extension or mix extension strategies.
Advertising is classified under place because it determines which warehouse stores the finished goods.
Altering existing products over time creates a new range instead of the previous one within alteration strategy.
Public relations is a product-mix contraction strategy that eliminates underperforming brands from the portfolio.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Personal selling is a promotional tool involving direct sales contact.
TRUE — Expansion uses either deeper lines or additional lines.
FALSE — Advertising is a promotional communication tool, not a distribution decision.
TRUE — Alteration replaces or refreshes an existing range when needs change.
FALSE — Public relations builds image within promotion; contraction eliminates products or lines.

title: Decline Stage Falling Sales
context: Consider a furniture retailer combining showroom display, home-delivery logistics, and finance instalment offers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Economies of scale in the growth stage always raise average unit costs as output increases.
Eliminating products or whole lines from the range reflects contraction within the product-mix strategy.
Cash cows receive the highest promotional investment because market growth in their segment remains rapid.
Stars no longer require promotional or production investment once they first achieve high market share.
A business may eliminate a product from its range when a relaunch does not seem promising.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Growth may lower average costs through economies of scale as output rises.
TRUE — Contraction removes products or lines that no longer fit the portfolio.
FALSE — Cash cows are in low-growth markets and usually receive lower promotional investment.
FALSE — Stars need continued investment in promotion and facilities to maintain position.
TRUE — Unpromising relaunch prospects can lead to product elimination.

title: BCG Matrix Relative Share and Growth
context: Review how stars combine strong market share with continued market growth. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Product-mix strategies include expansion, alteration, and contraction as shown in the textbook framework.
Product-mix contraction means adding new flavours within an existing ice-cream line to increase depth.
Specialising in one sort of product by offering just one product line narrows the product-mix width.
Diversifying production by offering different product lines increases the width of the product mix.
Increasing product-mix width means adding more variants within the same single product line only.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Expansion, alteration, and contraction are the three product-mix strategy groups.
FALSE — Adding flavours is line extension; contraction eliminates products or lines.
TRUE — Single-line specialisation keeps product-mix width narrow.
TRUE — Multiple lines diversify and widen the product mix.
FALSE — Width increases with more lines; depth increases variants within one line.

title: Question Marks in Growing Markets
context: Analyze cash cows as high-share products in markets with low growth. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Specialising in one product line diversifies the product mix by increasing the number of different lines offered.
A harmonised marketing mix can ignore customer needs in the targeted market if promotion spending is high enough.
Market research informs only the product P and has no role in price, place, or promotion decisions.
The product life cycle is a theoretical model of stages over a product's life span that differ in sales volume and profit.
Fad products typically remain in maturity for decades like detergents and toothpaste before any decline occurs.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Specialising narrows focus to one line; diversification adds different lines.
FALSE — The mix is designed to meet targeted customers' needs and wants, not ignore them.
FALSE — Market research underpins decisions across all four Ps.
TRUE — PLC stages vary in sales volume and profit over the product's life.
FALSE — Fads have short life cycles and may be withdrawn in under a year.

title: Stars and Strong Market Position
context: Consider a regional ice-cream producer adding new flavours within its existing range and later introducing a yogurt line. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Detergents and toothpaste are cited as examples of products with very short fad-like life cycles under one year.
Before market introduction there are no sales, yet product development costs mean the introduction phase starts with a loss.
After product launch, introductory prices may be low and heavy promotion may keep costs above sales early in introduction.
Towards the end of the introduction phase, revenues can exceed costs and a small profit may emerge.
During the growth period, sales increase more rapidly than costs and average costs may fall due to economies of scale.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — These products may have long or indefinite maturity phases, unlike fads.
TRUE — Pre-launch development costs create initial losses in introduction.
TRUE — Low intro prices and promotion spending can prolong introduction losses.
TRUE — Introduction can end with revenues surpassing costs for a modest profit.
TRUE — Growth brings faster sales gains and possible unit-cost reductions from scale.

title: Cash Cows in Low-Growth Markets
context: Analyze the price element of the marketing mix as the amount customers pay for the offering. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Adding yogurts beside an ice-cream line is classified as line extension rather than mix extension in the marketing-mix framework.
Business profit usually rises during the growth stage and peaks in the maturity stage of the product life cycle.
Changing packaging colours on an existing shampoo bottle is classified as relaunch rather than contraction in the marketing-mix framework.
Eliminating a weak product from the portfolio is classified as contraction rather than line extension in the marketing-mix framework.
Low share in a fast-growing market at launch is classified as question mark rather than cash cow in the marketing-mix framework.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Adding a new line is mix extension, not line extension.
TRUE — Profits typically grow through growth and peak at maturity.
FALSE — Packaging colour change is relaunch alteration, not contraction.
FALSE — Elimination is contraction, not line extension.
FALSE — That position is a question mark, not a cash cow.

title: Poor Dogs Near Decline
context: Review how introductory prices may be set low to attract customers at product launch. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: In the maturity stage, market growth slows while the product may still hold a high market share.
During decline, sales fall and profits fall, sometimes rapidly, as the product nears the end of its life cycle.
The duration of product life cycle stages varies enormously across different product categories.
High share when market growth has slowed is classified as cash cow rather than star in the marketing-mix framework.
Some products such as detergents, toothpaste, or perfumes may have a long or seemingly indefinite maturity phase.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Maturity combines slower market growth with often high share.
TRUE — Decline features falling sales and profits as the cycle ends.
TRUE — PLC length differs widely between product types.
FALSE — High share with low growth is a cash cow, not a star.
TRUE — Everyday products can remain in maturity for extended periods.

title: Price P and Customer Payments
context: Consider a start-up launching an innovative fitness tracker with heavy advertising, low introductory prices, and online-only sales. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: High share while the market is still growing is classified as star rather than poor dog in the marketing-mix framework.
Low share with low market growth near decline is classified as poor dog rather than question mark in the marketing-mix framework.
A low launch price to build market share quickly is classified as penetration pricing rather than price skimming in the marketing-mix framework.
Fad products may have a very short life cycle and be withdrawn in less than a year.
A high initial price later reduced over time is classified as price skimming rather than penetration pricing in the marketing-mix framework.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — High share with high growth is a star, not a poor dog.
FALSE — Low share and low growth define a poor dog.
FALSE — Low launch price for share is penetration, not skimming.
TRUE — Fads can complete their cycle and exit within months.
FALSE — High initial price is skimming, not penetration.

title: Introductory Low Pricing at Launch
context: Review penetration pricing as a strategy that sets a low price to gain market share quickly. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Increased competition in maturity often causes lower prices and higher promotional costs, pressuring profits.
The Boston Consulting Group matrix classifies products using relative market share and market growth.
A product with low relative market share in a rapidly growing market is classified as a question mark.
During introduction a product can be a question mark with low share in a growing market.
As market share rises in a still-growing market, a product may become a star in the BCG matrix.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Maturity competition can cut prices and raise promotion expense.
TRUE — BCG positions products by relative share and market growth.
TRUE — Low share plus high growth defines a question mark.
TRUE — Introduction-phase products may appear as question marks on the BCG matrix.
TRUE — Growing share in a growing market can produce a star.

title: Cost-Plus Pricing Markup Logic
context: Analyze price skimming as setting a high initial price before lowering it over time. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Stars are valuable because of their strong market position in a growing market.
Businesses invest in promotion and production facilities to maintain a star's strong position.
When market growth slows but market share remains high, a product may become a cash cow.
Cash cows usually receive lower investment because market growth has become low while revenues stay high.
As a product nears decline with low market growth and relatively low share, it increasingly becomes a poor dog.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Stars combine strength with continued market growth.
TRUE — Stars require ongoing promotional and capacity investment.
TRUE — High share with low growth characterises a cash cow.
TRUE — Low growth reduces investment needs while revenues remain substantial for cash cows.
TRUE — Low growth and low share near decline align with poor dogs.

title: Penetration Pricing for Market Share
context: Consider a beverage company using charm pricing on supermarket shelves and trade discounts for large retailers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Poor dogs combine low relative market share with low market growth in the BCG framework.
Stars occupy high relative market share combined with high market growth on the BCG matrix.
The price element of the marketing mix refers to the amount customers pay for the goods or services offered.
Affordable price is part of the basic marketing-mix idea alongside convenient place and promotional communication.
Introductory prices may be set low at product launch to attract customers during the introduction phase.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Poor dogs sit in the low-share, low-growth quadrant.
TRUE — High share and high growth define the star quadrant.
TRUE — Price is what customers pay for the business's offering.
TRUE — Affordable pricing supports the core mix objective of accessible value.
TRUE — Low launch prices help attract early customers in introduction.

title: Price Skimming on New Products
context: Analyze psychological pricing such as charm prices that influence customer perceptions. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Cost-plus pricing adds a markup to production costs when setting the selling price of a product.
Selling only through the firm's own shops is classified as direct distribution rather than indirect distribution in the marketing-mix framework.
Supplying supermarkets through a wholesaler is classified as indirect distribution rather than direct distribution in the marketing-mix framework.
Television commercials communicating product benefits is classified as advertising rather than place in the marketing-mix framework.
Penetration pricing sets a relatively low price to gain market share quickly after launch.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Cost-plus pricing builds price from costs plus a markup.
FALSE — Own shops illustrate direct, not indirect, distribution.
FALSE — Wholesaler routes are indirect, not direct, distribution.
FALSE — Television ads are promotion, not place.
TRUE — Penetration pricing uses low price to build share fast.

title: Competitive Pricing Against Rivals
context: Review discounts, payment terms, and allowances as tools within the price P. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Price skimming sets a high initial price that may be lowered later as competition increases.
Competitive pricing aligns the product's price with rival offerings in the same market.
Making a product available in supermarket aisles is classified as place rather than promotion in the marketing-mix framework.
Psychological pricing uses prices such as €9.99 to influence customer perceptions of affordability.
Discounts, payment terms, and trade allowances form part of the price tools within the marketing mix.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Skimming starts high and may reduce price over time.
TRUE — Competitive pricing references prices charged by competitors.
FALSE — Supermarket availability is place, not promotion.
TRUE — Charm prices like €9.99 are psychological pricing tools.
TRUE — Price P includes discounts, terms, and allowances.

title: Psychological Charm Pricing
context: Consider a book publisher selling through bookshops, online platforms, and direct school supply contracts. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: List price and negotiated trade discounts together shape the effective price paid by channel customers.
Sales representatives visiting business clients is classified as personal selling rather than public relations in the marketing-mix framework.
Price differentiation charges different prices to distinct customer groups or distribution channels.
Press releases building corporate reputation is classified as public relations rather than sales promotion in the marketing-mix framework.
A temporary price reduction during a sales event is a price decision linked to promotional activity.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Channel pricing combines list price with trade discounts.
FALSE — Visiting sales staff perform personal selling, not PR alone.
TRUE — Segment or channel differences can justify differentiated prices.
FALSE — PR builds image; sales promotion uses short-term incentives.
TRUE — Sale pricing interacts with promotional campaigns in the mix.

title: Discounts and Payment Terms
context: Review direct distribution where a business sells products without intermediaries to buyers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Finance instalment offers spread customer payments over time as part of the overall price package.
Loyalty discounts reward repeat customers and form part of the price element of the marketing mix.
Losses from development costs before sales take off is classified as introduction rather than maturity in the marketing-mix framework.
The place element of the marketing mix concerns where and how the product is made available to customers.
A convenient place for customers to buy supports the basic marketing-mix objective of accessible purchase.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Instalment terms shape how customers meet the price obligation.
TRUE — Loyalty discounts are price tools encouraging repeat purchase.
FALSE — Development losses occur in introduction, not maturity.
TRUE — Place covers distribution and customer access to the offering.
TRUE — Customer convenience in purchase location is central to place decisions.

title: Place P and Distribution Channels
context: Analyze indirect distribution through wholesalers and retailers to reach final consumers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Rapid sales increases with falling average costs is classified as growth rather than decline in the marketing-mix framework.
Profit peaking while market growth slows is classified as maturity rather than introduction in the marketing-mix framework.
Falling sales and profits as demand weakens is classified as decline rather than growth in the marketing-mix framework.
Place decisions focus on customer access and distribution channels rather than the firm's own office location.
Direct distribution sells products to customers without using intermediaries such as wholesalers or retailers.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Rapid sales growth characterises growth, not decline.
FALSE — Profit peak with slower growth fits maturity, not introduction.
FALSE — Falling sales and profits indicate decline, not growth.
TRUE — Place is about reaching customers, not where the firm is headquartered.
TRUE — Direct distribution bypasses intermediaries between producer and buyer.

title: Direct Distribution Without Intermediaries
context: Consider a furniture retailer combining showroom display, home-delivery logistics, and finance instalment offers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Indirect distribution uses intermediaries such as wholesalers and retailers to reach final consumers.
Wholesalers purchase products in bulk and resell them to retailers within a distribution channel.
Retailers make products available to end customers at shops, supermarkets, or other points of sale.
Online sales platforms can serve as a place channel alongside physical shops for the same product.
Selling through own shops is an example of direct distribution within the place element of the mix.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Intermediaries carry products to end customers in indirect distribution.
TRUE — Wholesalers bulk-buy and supply retailers downstream.
TRUE — Retailers provide final customer access in the channel.
TRUE — E-commerce complements physical outlets within place strategy.
TRUE — Own retail outlets exemplify direct distribution.

title: Indirect Distribution Through Retailers
context: Analyze how retailers make products available to end customers at the point of purchase. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Supplying supermarkets through a wholesaler illustrates indirect distribution in the place P.
Intensive distribution places products in many outlets to maximise convenience for customers.
Selective distribution limits the number of outlets to protect brand positioning and service standards.
Exclusive distribution uses a very limited number of specialised partners to sell the product.
Home-delivery logistics extend place convenience after a customer purchases from a showroom.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Wholesaler-to-retailer routes show indirect distribution.
TRUE — Wide outlet coverage reflects intensive distribution.
TRUE — Fewer selected outlets characterise selective distribution.
TRUE — Exclusive arrangements restrict outlet numbers sharply.
TRUE — Delivery services extend place convenience beyond the initial outlet.

title: Wholesaler Role in Distribution
context: Review online sales channels as part of place decisions alongside physical outlets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Distribution channel analysis can reveal weaknesses and encourage alternative channels in place planning.
The promotion element of the marketing mix covers communicating a message in order to promote the sale of the product.
Advertising informs and persuades target customers as a promotional tool within the marketing mix.
Because breakfast cereals are physical goods, services such as installation or support cannot be counted in the product P for that business.
A global breakfast cereals brand guarantees that product quality may vary sharply between countries without affecting brand recognition.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Channel review supports place improvements and alternatives.
TRUE — Promotion communicates messages that encourage product sales.
TRUE — Advertising is a core promotional communication tool.
FALSE — The product P includes services as well as goods offered by the business.
FALSE — Brands serve as a guarantee of stable quality maintained across markets.

title: Retailer Access for Final Customers
context: Consider a regional ice-cream producer adding new flavours within its existing range and later introducing a yogurt line. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Selling breakfast cereals exclusively through wholesalers means the business uses direct distribution with no intermediaries.
Sales promotion includes short-term incentives and sales events designed to stimulate purchase.
Personal selling involves direct contact between sales staff and customers to promote the product.
Public relations activities build a favourable image of the business or brand among stakeholders.
Setting a low introductory price for new breakfast cereals is an example of price skimming aimed only at early luxury buyers.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Wholesaler channels indicate indirect distribution, not direct.
TRUE — Sales events and incentives belong to sales promotion.
TRUE — Face-to-face selling is personal selling within promotion.
TRUE — PR shapes favourable perceptions as part of promotion.
FALSE — Low introductory pricing aligns with penetration or launch pricing, not skimming.

title: Online and Physical Place Channels
context: Review the promotion element of the marketing mix as communicating a message to promote sales. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Removing an outdated breakfast cereals model after failed relaunch attempts is an example of product-mix expansion through mix extension.
Businesses may spend heavily on promotion through advertisements and sales events during product introduction.
A breakfast cereals product with high market share in a no-growth market is a question mark requiring maximum market-growth investment.
Promotional spending in the growth stage helps maintain a star product's strong market position.
Cash-cow products in low-growth markets usually receive lower promotional investment than stars.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Elimination after failed relaunch is contraction, not expansion.
TRUE — Introduction often features substantial advertising and sales-event spending.
FALSE — High share in a low-growth market is a cash cow, not a question mark.
TRUE — Growth-stage promotion supports stars' competitive position.
TRUE — Low-growth cash cows need less promotional spending than stars.

title: Customer Access Not Firm Location
context: Analyze advertising as a promotional tool that informs and persuades target customers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Window displays and social-media campaigns are promotional tools communicating the product message.
Brochure advertising and reservation campaigns can coordinate promotion with price and place decisions.
A sales force calling on business customers is part of the promotion mix for organisational buyers.
Promotional messages should reflect the needs of the targeted segment identified through market research.
Increased competition near decline may raise promotional costs as firms fight for remaining demand.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Displays and social media carry promotional messages.
TRUE — Brochures and campaigns integrate promotion with other Ps.
TRUE — B2B personal selling is a promotional tool for business markets.
TRUE — Segment needs guide promotional messaging content.
TRUE — Late-cycle competition can push promotional spending higher.

title: Promotion P and Communicating Messages
context: Consider a start-up launching an innovative fitness tracker with heavy advertising, low introductory prices, and online-only sales. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

A relaunch with updated packaging can refresh appeal among small-business owners without launching an entirely new product line.
Line extension with a budget variant can attract small-business owners within an existing product line without widening the whole mix.
A separate business unit supplying mobile-device components may address a distinct segment with its own product characteristics and cycle.
Portfolio analysis may classify mobile-device components as a question mark, star, cash cow, or poor dog depending on share and growth.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Complex offers to small-business owners can benefit from personal selling.
TRUE — Packaging relaunch can renew interest among small-business owners within alteration strategy.
TRUE — Budget variants for small-business owners deepen the line through line extension.
TRUE — mobile-device components units can target different segments with tailored products.
TRUE — mobile-device components can map to different BCG categories by market conditions.

title: Doctor Personal Selling Promotion
context: Analyze how a question mark arises from low relative share in a rapidly growing market. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A product line aimed at young families must contain unrelated categories such as food and machinery to count as one line.
Market research on commuters informs only promotion decisions and cannot influence product, price, or place choices.
A familiar brand offers no reassurance to commuters because brands belong exclusively to the promotion P.
Technical support services related to mobile-device components count as products within the product element of the marketing mix.
Low introductory pricing aimed at commuters is classified as product-mix contraction because it reduces revenue per unit.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — A product line contains similar products, even when targeting young families.
FALSE — Market research underpins decisions across all four Ps, including for commuters.
FALSE — Brands support product differentiation and can reassure commuters, not only promotion.
TRUE — Support for mobile-device components is a product offering, not merely promotion.
FALSE — Introductory low pricing is a price decision, not product-mix contraction.
